```{python}
#| echo: false

import sys
from pathlib import Path

# Ensure root-level modules (scripts/) are importable in both Quarto run contexts.
cwd = Path.cwd()
project_root = cwd if (cwd / "scripts").exists() else cwd.parent
if str(project_root) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(project_root))

# Convention: keep the workbook at data/raw/workbook.xlsx.
CHA_WORKBOOK_PATH = project_root / "data" / "raw" / "workbook.xlsx"
```

## How this works

The figures and table below are **not hand-written**. They are generated from the
indicator sheets in `data/raw/workbook.xlsx`. On every `quarto render`, the
`pre-render` hook in `_quarto.yml` runs `scripts/generate_chapter_objects.py`,
which writes one include file per object into `chapters/_generated/objects/`.
This chapter just pulls them in.

The same `Example Indicator` sheet renders as both a bar figure (@fig-example) and a
table (@tbl-example), and a second `Example Trend` sheet renders as a line figure
(@fig-example-trend).

## To add your own indicator

Each indicator is one sheet in the workbook (the flat per-indicator format used by
the Mid-Hudson CHA). To add one:

1. Copy an example sheet (`Example Indicator` or `Example Trend`).
2. Set the config cells in column A/B: `Name`, `Table/Figure/Both`, `Object ID`,
   `Figure Type`, `X Column`, etc.
3. Fill the data block to the right of the `Enter Data` cell (row-label column plus
   value columns, with per-column format codes in the row above).
4. Reference it in any chapter with `{{< include _generated/objects/<object_id>.qmd >}}`
   (for example `fig-<id>` or `tbl-<id>`).
5. Run `quarto render` - the include file regenerates automatically.

See `scripts/WORKBOOK_SCHEMA.md` and `scripts/PIPELINE_USAGE.md` for full details.
